notes.residency_days_threshold: A resident individual is a person who has a permanent home in Uganda; or is present in Uganda: for a period of 183 days or more in any twelve (12) months period that commences or ends during the year of income; or during the year of income and in each of the two preceding years of income, for periods averaging 122 days in each such year of income; or is an employee or official of the government of Uganda posted abroad during the year of income.
notes.bik_housing_employment_income_rate: Accommodation/housing: the lesser of: a) the market rent of the accommodation or housing reduced by any payment made by the employee for the benefit; or b) 15% of the employment income, including the amount referred to in paragraph (a), paid by the employer to the employee for the year of income. Benefits in kind are added to employment income and are subject to PAYE.
notes.bik_motor_vehicle_inclusion_rate: Motor vehicle: (20% x A x B/C) - D where A is the market value of the motor vehicle at the time when it was first provided for the private use of the employee, depreciated on a reducing balance basis at a rate of 35% per annum for the subsequent years; B is the number of days in the year of income in which the motor vehicle was used or available for use for private purposes; C is the number of days in the year of income; D is any payment made by the employee for the benefit.
notes.withholding_non_resident_service_contrac: A Ugandan-sourced service contract does not include an employment contract (Withholding-Tax-FY-2024-25-1.pdf).
notes.excise_duty_mobile_money_withdrawal: Excise duty of 0.5% applies to cash withdrawals from mobile money. Transfers and deposits are not charged this 0.5% withdrawal duty.
notes.presumptive_tax_upper_threshold: Businesses with annual gross turnover between UGX 10,000,000 and UGX 150,000,000 qualify for the presumptive tax regime. Above UGX 150,000,000, standard corporate or individual income tax rules apply.
notes.penal_tax_late_filing_monthly_rate: Penal tax for failure to furnish a tax return by the due date is UGX 200,000 or 2% of the tax payable per month (or part of a month) that the return remains unfiled, whichever is greater.
notes.paye_bands_resident: Schedule 4 Part I states ANNUAL chargeable income; these are the monthly equivalents (annual divided by 12). The Act's table is: nil up to UGX 4,020,000; 20% of the excess over 4,020,000 up to 4,920,000; UGX 180,000 plus 25% of the excess over 4,920,000 up to 5,820,000; UGX 405,000 plus 30% of the excess over 5,820,000 up to 120,000,000; above 120,000,000 the same plus an additional 10% of the excess over 120,000,000. The top band is expressed here as a single 40% marginal rate.
notes.paye_bands_non_resident: The 2026 Act substitutes only Schedule 4 Part I, which by its terms applies to resident individuals. Part II (non-residents) is not amended, so the Cap 338 rates continue to apply.
notes.withholding_royalty: The 2026 Act amends only the s.2 definition of 'royalty' (inserting 'software'); it does not change the rate. The 15% here is the pre-existing Cap 338 rate and has not been reconciled against s.83 directly.
notes.withholding_non_business_asset: Applies to a person who purchases a non-business asset (s.130(3)). Distinct from the 6% on services and goods under s.119.
notes.withholding_telecom_commission: Commission paid by a telecommunications service provider for telecom retail services, mobile network services or mobile money services.
notes.rental_tax_individual: The 2026 Act (s.12, inserting s.124(1a)) lets an individual liable to rental tax file a provisional return monthly. The rate and annual threshold are unchanged.
notes.vat_registration_threshold_annual: Businesses below UGX 300,000,000 annual turnover are no longer required to register; voluntary registration remains available.
notes.customs_duty_common: Indicative EAC CET band for finished consumer goods. The binding rate is the tariff line for the specific HS code.
